last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Wed 08-19, day 8 in country, lunch anchor. DEEP-DIVE, and the break contract was paid at the door for the first time since he called it out — I opened on the kol tail (eduthukka = edu + kol, the swallowed verb "to hold onto yourself"; why the translator renders naane paathukkaren as "I will see myself"; the -e on naane as the teeth). THREE COLD AND UNAIDED, ALL INSIDE ONE SENTENCE HE BUILT HIMSELF. Athai told the room he does not eat spice; before I had handed him anything he produced "illa, konjam kaaram pidikkum". kaaram and pidikkum had never been drilled and came out of his own pocket; naalaiku landed clean and unprompted later. HINTED, NOT FIRES — do not read these as wins: appadi illa, mudinja, appuram. I gave him the appadi illa upgrade (illa contradicts HER, appadi illa corrects the PICTURE) and he echoed it back in ten seconds, but it has still never fired unaided. That is the check to run next. TWO REPEATED SLIPS, BOTH LIVE. english-word-order hit a THIRD time — "enna nalaiku samayal" for "naalaiku enna samayal" — and I carved it for the first time by laying all three instances side by side (07-27, 08-10, today): one rule, Tamil sets the stage (when/where) first and asks last, English leads with the question word. That carve IS the format change the escalation demanded; the next dose is a SOAK, never another episode, because this pattern has never been poured into his ear. sinna-for-konjam recurred at 15 days ("kutti kaaram") and HE NAMED THE GAP HIMSELF, unprompted: "I will still need to work on when to select each." He got the first real tool that item has ever had — the opposite-word test: if the opposite is periya it is chinna, if the opposite is romba it is konjam. AND HE DID THE RIGHT THING UNDER PRESSURE: told to ask Athai what she is cooking, he looked up samayal and built a NOUN question, dodging the verb entirely. That is the Noun Shortcut firing on instinct, not on instruction — credited out loud, with samaikkireenga and the -eenga register point handed over for later. SPOON MISSION UNFIRED — SECOND MISSION RUNNING TO DIE FOR WANT OF AN OPENING. His words: "no opening and I am still working on this one." The 08-15 line died exactly the same way. That is my design fault twice, not his failure, so I widened the trigger live: naane eduthukkaren needs no ladle and no dinner, only any object moving toward him that he could carry himself — plate, jug, bag, chair. STILL OPEN: the repair-line drill is produced and still unconsumed; bluff-not-repair sits at 2x. Amma birthday ~Aug 24 — pirandha naal vazhthukkal is SEEN only, has never once left his mouth, four days out. I trailed tomorrow on it explicitly: that line cannot be improvised on the day.

soak_order.focus: FORMAT CHANGE for english-word-order (3x over 23d, escalated). It has had an episode and slipped again; it has never had a SOAK. IMPORTANT FRAMING, corrected live 08-19: this is NEUTRAL vs MARKED, not right vs wrong. Tamil scrambles freely before the verb; what is fixed is verb-last, and what is merely DEFAULT is when/where up front with the question word hugging the verb. So do not teach, do not explain, do not name the rule and never imply the other order is an error — just pour the unmarked shape into his ear until front-loading the question word feels wrong to him on its own. Permute the stage-first slot: naalaiku enna samaikkireenga? / ippo enna panreenga? / apparam sollunga / hotel-la nirthunga / tamizh-la eppadi solradhu? / veetla yaaru irukkanga? Time words, place words, -la and -ku phrases, all in first position, many voices, many speeds. Never two consecutive lines with the same opener, and not one line with the question word fronted — not even as a contrast. Passive: he listens, nothing is demanded.
